2. 1 Kotwali, District Durg (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Section 420, 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: 3. Applicants namely; Vishal Malhotra in MCRCA No.1642/2022, and Nagendra Somankar and Raju Ghongdhe in MCRCA No.1727/2022.

4. The prosecution story, in brief, is that the complainant namely Anand Bafna has made a written complaint against the present applicant that he sold a land to the present applicant along with the other purchasers, of Rs.66,00,000/- and also gave him cheques of total amount of Rs.16,60,000/-
from his ICICI Bank Ltd. and requested him to present the cheques before the bank in the month of April 2022 but due to insufficient balance, the cheques were dishonored.
Thereafter, a case was registered against the applicant and other co-accused persons for the aforesaid offences.
5. Learned counsel for the applicants submit that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
She further submits that complainant deposited the cheques in the bank without informing the applicant and other co-accused persons.
She further submits that complainant had bad intention to earn more money from the applicants, therefore, the applicants may kindly be granted anticipatory bail.
6. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the bail application.

7. Learned counsel for the Objector submits that some amount has been paid by the applicants, but still some amount have to be paid by the applicants, so this application is liable to be dismissed.
8.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the intervenor submits that whole consideration amount has been paid by the applicants, therefore, he has no objection.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

10. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and having considered the submission made by the parties, nature of allegation, without commenting anything on the merits of the case,
the present are considered to be a fit cases to release the applicants on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

11. It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicants in connection with crime in question, they shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting them on their executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- each with one local surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer with following conditions :
(i) that they shall make themselves available for interrogation before Investigating Officer as and when required;
(ii) that they shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of case so as to dissuade him /her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
Nagendra Somankar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167170391/
2 (iii) that they shall not act, in any manner, which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial; and (iv) that they shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
Sd/-
(Rajani Dubey) Judge Deepti Jha Nagendra Somankar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167170391/
